title: Intensive Russian Fundamentals
description: First half of first‐year Russian in a time‐intensive form. Development of meaningful communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with Russian speakers and beginning study of Russian. Learner‐centered approach develops speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.
prerequisites_raw: Placement into RUSSIAN 1A

title: Fundamentals of Russian
description: Focuses on reading, comprehension, basic composition, and conversation skills, and gives the student an initial exposure to the Russian cultural scene.
prerequisites_raw: RUSSIAN 1A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 1B is also accepted

title: Intensive Russian Fundamentals
description: Second half of first‐year Russian in a time‐intensive form. Development of meaningful communicative skills for the purposes of interaction with Russian speakers and beginning study of Russian. Learner‐centered approach develops speaking, listening, reading, writing, and cultural skills and knowledge.
prerequisites_raw: RUSSIAN 1AB with a minimum grade of C or RUSSIAN 1B with a minimum grade of C

title: Fundamentals of Russian
description: Focuses on reading, comprehension, basic composition, and conversation skills, and gives the student an initial exposure to the Russian cultural scene.
prerequisites_raw: RUSSIAN 1AB with a minimum grade of C or RUSSIAN 1B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 1C is also accepted

title: Intermediate Russian
description: Students read simple passages from contemporary Russian literary texts and newspapers. Development of oral skills and exposure to Russian culture continue.
prerequisites_raw: RUSSIAN 1BC with a minimum grade of C or RUSSIAN 1C with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 2A is also accepted

title: Intermediate Russian
description: Students read simple passages from contemporary Russian literary texts and newspapers. Development of oral skills and exposure to Russian culture continue.
prerequisites_raw: RUSSIAN 2A with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 2B is also accepted

title: Intermediate Russian
description: Students read simple passages from contemporary Russian literary texts and newspapers. Development of oral skills and exposure to Russian culture continue.
prerequisites_raw: RUSSIAN 2B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into RUSSIAN 2C is also accepted

title: Topics in Russian Culture
description: Study of varied topics in Russian culture, area studies, and society, both in the present and in historical perspective.

title: Special Studies Russian
description: Special studies under faculty supervision.

title: Writing About Russian Literature
description: Requires at least 4,000 words of assigned composition based upon readings in Russian literature (in English translation), culture, and society. Several essays required.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Topics in Russian Literature
description: Examines major themes in Russian literature, film, and other media from the eighteenth to twenty-first centuries. Taught in English.

title: Topics in Russian Language Through Film
description: Uses Russian films of the late 20th century to enhance students' language skills and deepen their cultural knowledge. Work involves intensive conversation, reading and listening comprehension, and the acquisition of written skills and grammatical accuracy. Conducted primarily in Russian.
prerequisites_raw: RUSSIAN 2C (may be taken concurrently)

title: Principles in the Social Sciences
description: Introduction to various disciplines within the social sciences. Provides an interdisciplinary perspective on understanding human behavior and social institutions, including interpersonal, economic, and cultural activities.

title: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H1E or SOCECOL H20A

title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H1F or SOCECOL H20B

title: Introduction to Social Science Analysis
description: Introduction to social science research and analytical models. Theory construction and use of research methods in an interdisciplinary context. Discussion of the application of social science research to public policy. Computer laboratories develop creative thinking, graphing, and data presentation skills.

title: Computer-Based Research in the Social Sciences
description: Focuses on the data manipulation, data visualization, and information searching techniques. Hands-on experience in hypothesis testing, mapping, graphics, and data arrays.

title: Introduction to Global Studies
description: Ongoing historical processes that increase global integration, the social, economic, and political interdependence of different regions, cultures, and peoples. Topics include ancient empires, colonialism, nationalism, industrialization, modern imperialism and warfare, decolonization, global social movements, conflict, inequality, and global governance.

title: Introduction to Human Geography
description: Human behavior in a geographical context. Spatial patterns and organization of the cultural, social, and economic activities of man as imposed on and influenced by the earth's physical setting.

title: Introduction to Physical Geography
description: An introduction to the physical world we live in. Distribution and dynamics of the earth's air, water, and solid crust. Concepts and principles from climatology and geology. Selected examples from North America and beyond.

title: US and World Geography
description: Survey of general geographical principles and facts on a world scale, as well as introduction to the broad regional and resource geography of the U.S., emphasizing in particular the interactions of physical and cultural factors.

title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences I
description: Introduction to the variety of statistical applications in the social sciences. Descriptive statistics. Measures of central tendency and dispersion. Percentile ranks. Standardization and normal approximation. Basic probability theory focuses on application to statistical inference and binomial distribution. Laboratory required.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 3A

title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences II
description: Introduction to statistical inference, sampling distribution, standard error. Hypothesis tests for proportions and means. Inferential techniques for nominal variables including chi-square, study measures of strengths, significance of relationships between variables, assumptions, data requirements, and types of error in significance tests.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 10A

title: Probability and Statistics in Social Sciences III
description: Focus on correlation, regression, and control for effects of variables. One-way and two-way factorial analysis of variance. A priori and a posteriori comparisons. Introduction to repeated measures design and non-parametric statistics. Discuss use of statistics in newspapers and popular magazines.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 10B

title: Global Political Ideologies
description: An overview of the major political ideologies shaping the current world order and global conflict. Topics include liberalism, democracy, nationalism, capitalism, communism, socialism, fascism, neoliberalism, clash of civilizations, sectarian violence, populist nationalism, and de-globalization.

title: Global Political Economy
description: The global economy as an integrated system. The rise of world trade, capitalism, national economies, market cycles, competing economic ideologies, development, globalization, transnational labor, multinational corporations, and the role of UN, World Bank, WTO, and the IMF in global governance.

title: Human Rights and Global Governance
description: Historical development of civil, political rights and the rise of human rights in international law. Explores role, and limitations, of the UN, ICJ, and ICC in global governance. Reconceptualizing democracy and political representation in a postnational 21st century.

title: Global Environmental Issues
description: Examines problems such as global climate change, growing human populations, fisheries depletion, ocean acidification, biodiversity loss, deforestation, and food security. Introduces political, social, and economic factors contributing to environmental issues and their disproportional impacts on the world’s poor and minorities.

title: AI Literacy
description: Introduction to the basics of contemporary artificial intelligence. Distinction between symbolic and neural AIs. Generative AI, prediction engines, recommendation systems, machine perception. Near-term ethical issues, medium-term economic implications, long-term risk, and safety.

title: Social Policy and Public Service
description: An introduction to the basic theories and principles of public policy. Students examine various influences on the development of public policy and the principle actors in the process, and learn to identify tools and techniques employed in policy making.

title: Introduction to Gangs
description: Introduces students to street gang subculture and explores risk factors associated with gang membership. Students develop a working definition for street gang and understand the difference between social and legal definitions. Also explores the connection between prison and street gangs.

title: Comparing Cultures
description: Introduces students to the scope of cross-cultural comparisons by analyzing the theories, methodologies, and facts utilized by anthropologists, sociologists, social psychologists, political scientists, and historians in comparing cultures.

title: Asian American Histories
description: Examines and compares diverse experiences of major Asian American groups since the mid-nineteenth century. Topics include origins of emigration; the formation and transformation of community; gender and family life; changing roles of Asian Americans in American society. Formerly ASIANAM 60A.

title: Asian American Communities
description: Examines the renewal of Asian immigration following World War II. Explores contemporary Asian American populations and communities in the U.S., and the impact of contemporary Asian immigration on the U.S. political economy and social order.

title: Asian Americans and Race
description: Analyzes the Asian American experience in comparative perspective, which includes comparisons of different ethnic and racial groups, and across gender and class. Possible topics include labor, economy, politics, migration, nation, popular culture, gender, family, sexuality, and multiraciality.

title: Special Topics in Social Sciences
description: Studies in selected areas of Social Sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems in Social Sciences
description: Hands-on laboratory course introduces students to the fundamentals of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) technology using social science applications. Students learn to organize, manipulate, and display spatial data leading to the design of their own GIS research project.

title: Intermediate Geographic Information Systems in Social Sciences
description: Expands Geographic Information Systems (GIS) skills to more advanced theories and concepts in the spatial analysis of social science issues and particularly to analyzing and interpreting spatial data. Students develop and complete a GIS research project of their own choosing.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 102A

title: Game Theory and Politics I
description: Introduction to game theory and a survey of its political applications. Examples of topics covered include voting in small committees, legislatures, and mass elections; interest group activities and environmental issues; institutional design, and the evolution of cooperative behavior.

title: International Business
description: Introduction to conducting business in the international arena, decision-making in the organization, and globalization of markets and production. Topics covered range from tax and finance to ethics, marketing, and more. Continuing corporate regulatory scandals discussed.

title: Special Topics in Geography
description: Studies in selected areas of geography. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Transnational Gangs
description: Examines the internationalization of U.S. domestic street gangs. The relationship between California gangs Mara Salvatrucha and 18th Street and Mexico/Central American gangs is assessed. Specified topics include: mobilization, migration, territorialism, culture, organization, and use of technology.

title: Voting and Political Manipulation
description: Introduction to social choice and cooperative games. Topics include majority rule, types of voting methods, apportionment and proportional representation, agenda manipulation, coalition formation, voting power, political consequences of electoral laws.

title: Veterans in History and Society
description: Explores key concepts, issues, and trends in the interdisciplinary field of veterans studies. Students gain a deep understanding of the ways that social scientists and historians have analyzed the identities, experiences, and worldviews of U.S. military veterans.

title: Veterans’ Transitions
description: Provides veteran and non-veteran students with a comprehensive and academically rigorous overview of the ways and means through which diverse communities of veterans have made and continue to make the complex and multi-faceted transition from active military.

title: Veterans’ Voices
description: Uses the medium of academic writing to develop a broad understanding and appreciation for the wide range of worldviews, priorities, and values embodied in the creative production and activism of diverse U.S. military veterans.

title: International Humanitarianism
description: Examines, analyzes, and evaluates the humanitarian phenomenon, the actors involved in it (including states, international organizations (IOs), and nongovernmental organizations (NGOs)), the rise of a body of international humanitarian law, and the problems and debates associated with international humanitarianism today.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Non-Government Organization (NGO) Fundamentals
description: Introduction to non-governmental organizations, including their role in U.S. society and the international community. Explores varying definitions of NGOs and the characteristics held in common by all NGOs.

title: American Public Policy
description: Focuses on the development and implementation of public policy in the United States. Lectures cover theoretical models of the policy process as well as significant problems facing contemporary American decision-makers.

title: Leadership Through Mentorship
description: A mentor driven forum, features lectures and discussions by professional leaders highlighting effective leadership styles, narratives, and accomplishments. Students learn different leadership methods and gain insight to their own professional aspirations.

title: Race in the City: Past, Present, and Future
description: Students examine the historical, social, political, and economic factors that contributed to the construction of the American urban context, one that is poverty concentrated and racially/ethnically segregated. Students also critically assess the consequence of growing up in America's urban neighborhoods.

title: Chicane/Latine Education
description: Provides a historical and empirical overview of educational issues affecting diverse Latine low-income, immigrant, and U.S. born student populations enrolled in American schools. Examines policies and issues such as DACA, generation, culture, racism, and gender on educational mobility.

title: Domestic Gangs
description: Examines the history and development of California street gangs and the role of historical events in that development. Students will be able to contrast and compare gang cohort behaviors between some of the major gangs in California.

title: Prison Gangs
description: Examines the growth and spread of prison gangs throughout the country. Relationships between prison and street gangs, and possible relationships with foreign drug trafficking organizations studied. Violence examined as the standard to establish dominance in and out of prison.

title: Juvenile Gangs
description: Examines risk factors that can be used to predict gang membership. Compares generational with non-generational gangs and develops a working sociological definition that can be used to identify street gangs. Myths about juveniles, street gangs.

title: Chicano/Latino Families
description: Introduction to the research, literature, and issues surrounding the topic of Chicano/Latino families including cultural history, contemporary issues, organization of family, traditions, lifestyles, values, beliefs, generational differences, gender issues, ethnic identity, evolution of demographic patterns, current economic and political standings.

title: Immigration and Inequality
description: Explores immigration, ethnicity, and inequality as interconnected social forces. International migration, propelled by global inequalities, plays a central role in the formation of multinational societies, shapes inter-group relations and patterns of ethnic inequality, and transforms the immigrants themselves.

title: Research Methods in the Social Sciences
description: Examines how interdisciplinary social science research questions are formulated and studies several research methods including: experimental method, quasi-experimental methods, survey research, field research, evaluation research, and meta-analysis. Parametric and non-parametric statistical methods are illustrated using the SPSS program.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 1A and SOC SCI 2A and SOC SCI 3A and ( SOC SCI 10A or STATS 7 )

title: American Culture
description: A survey of the historical development of dominant American culture and society; emphasis on a close reading of key cultural texts, with weekly text as a model of writing, examining its use of language and rhetoric.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Revolution in Latin America
description: Presents a comparative analysis of the causes, development, and consequences of selected revolutionary movements, focusing on outbreaks in Mexico, Bolivia, Cuba, Chile, Nicaragua, and Grenada. Explores topics of state formation, economic nationalism, social justice, ethnicity, and role of international affairs.

title: Asian American Women
description: Examines the representations and experiences of Asian American women from diverse perspectives. Explores the commonalities and differences among various groups of Asian American women, with particular focus on history, culture, values, and family roles.

title: Korean American Studies
description: Explores the factors that have distinctly shaped the Korean American experience, including patterns of racial domination, the profile of immigrant flow, immigrant roles in the urban political economy, politics in Korea, and the role of the church.

title: Vietnamese American Studies
description: Studies the resettlement of Vietnamese in the United States following their exodus from Southeast Asia. Topics include the Vietnam War, the 1975 evacuation, boat and land refugees, the shaping of Vietnamese communities, and Vietnamese American literature.

title: Japanese American Studies
description: Studies the settlement of Japanese in Hawaii and the continental United States since the late 19th century. Topics include sugar plantations, development of rural Japanese America, World War II internment, post-War community development, and persistence of Japanese American identity.

title: South Asian American Studies
description: Examines and compares the experiences of South Asian immigrants in the U.S. over time. Looks at the economic, political, and social positions of the immigrants, with special emphasis on religious changes and the changes in the second and later generations.

title: Southeast Asian American Studies
description: Analyzes experiences of refugees and immigrants from Southeast Asia, which may include those from Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, and the Philippines. Examines political and economic factors for their exodus and how they reconstruct their identities, histories, and communities.

title: Filipina/Filipino American Studies
description: Explores the experience of Filipina/Filipino Americans from the era of Spanish colonization of the Philippines to present-day community formations in the United States, with special emphasis on the 20th century. Topics include colonialism, nation, migration, gender, and culture.

title: Special Topics in Asian American Studies
description: Studies in selected areas of Asian American Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Summer Program in Research and Leadership A
description: Builds understanding of computational research methods and project design using diverse information sources. Focuses on social science statistics, including exploratory and descriptive analysis, chi-square, correlation, regression, and multiple regression techniques for applied research interpretation and practice.

title: Summer Program in Research and Leadership B
description: Introduces theories and methods for quantitative and qualitative research in social sciences and humanities. Students develop research interests, design original proposals, apply methods like ethnography and statistics, conduct ethical fieldwork, and connect theory, methodology, and critical analysis.

title: Summer Program in Research and Leadership C
description: Explores the transformative potential of graduate education. Students engage with texts, guest speakers, and workshops on mentorship, work-life balance, and graduate preparation while developing personal statements, relationships, and professional pathways across academia, public service, law, and consulting.

title: Ethical Leadership
description: Explores historical and contemporary theories of ethical and unethical leadership. Examines models of "good leadership" such as cardinal and monastic virtues; and models of "bad leadership," such as Machiavelli's Prince. Explores the philosophies, styles, and accomplishments of leaders.

title: Global and International Studies Forum
description: A faculty-student forum featuring lectures from a variety of institutions with discussion issues related to Global and International Studies.

title: Seminar Conflict Resolution
description: Designed for seniors who are pursuing the International Studies major and/or minor. Provides a forum in which students will refine skills and theory in the study of cooperation and conflict, from local to global arenas. Students write research paper.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Conflict Resolution in Cross-Cultural Perspective
description: Examines theories of conflict management. Analyzes how conflict is mitigated in diverse cultures: at the interpersonal level, between groups, and on the international scale. Students discuss readings, hear from conflict management practitioners, and simulate negotiations.

title: Sage Leader Research I
description: Participants in the SAGE Scholars Program learn to define leadership concepts, discover various leadership styles, and develop strong leadership and communication skills resulting in strengthened ability to contribute to and interact with UCI and the Orange County community.

title: Sage Leader Research II
description: Provides a survey of contemporary topics and challenges in the fields of management and leadership. Case studies and text by leading authors are used to analyze key leadership issues in twenty-first century, with particular emphasis on current events.

title: Media Writing
description: Designed to teach reporting and news writing basics. Students learn how to gather and organize information, ask effective questions, develop story ideas, research facts, and write stories on deadline.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: People in Society
description: Through readings about people in distinctly different societies throughout history, students learn concepts that cross the boundaries of the social science disciplines. Such themes as democracy, elitism, power, social class, and gender are the basis for discussion and writing.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Twenty-First-Century Graduate Education
description: Graduate and professional education in twenty-first century United States. Examines strategies for admission to postbaccalaureate programs and success in graduate study culture. Introduction to processes including planning and preparation, school selection, entrance examination preparation, submission of applications, writing personal statements.

title: Introduction to Contemporary Middle East Politics
description: An overview of basic issues that shape the politics of the Middle East and North Africa. Themes include implication of the colonization era, nation-state formation, inter-Arab relations, nationalism, Arab-Israel conflict, Islamic resurgence, and more.

title: Arab Uprisings
description: Examines political mobilization against authoritarian rule in individual Arab countries, explaining specific outcome in each. Addresses the movement’s second wind nearly a decade later, which affected a new subset of Arab countries.

title: Political Islam
description: Political Islamd is a diverse phenomenon. While noticeable barriers exist to "Islamist democracy," it is the Islamists who will define the political future of much of the Muslim world. Reviews the experience of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey, and Indonesia.

title: Special Topics in Social Sciences
description: Studies in selected areas of social sciences. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Honors Research Workshop
description: Student develops a 10–15-page prospectus of research for the honors thesis which includes: the research question, literature review, methods of investigation, and bibliography. Student selects a faculty mentor who will supervise thesis research and writing in winter and spring.

title: Honors Thesis Research
description: The student initiates and completes data collection for the honors thesis. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H190A or SPPS H190A

title: Honors Thesis
description: The student completes, with the approval of the faculty mentor, an honors thesis containing: statement of the problem, literature review, research hypotheses, methods of investigation, results, discussion, and bibliography.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H190B or SPPS H190B . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 70C or SOCIOL 63 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and underserved communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 193A

title: Field Studies in Social Policy and Public Service
description: Advanced training in qualitative and ethnographic research centered on community service. Students pursue field studies at nonprofit agencies (200 hours) to understand current social problems in underrepresented and under-served communities. Through field placement, students apply theory to practice.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 193B

title: Public Service Internship
description: Introduces the role of etiquette and leadership in the professional environment. With a two-unit (50 hours) or four-unit (100 hours) credit option, students intern at a nonprofit agency exploring their roles as community leaders and improving their professional skills.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Management and Leadership Practicum-Social Science
description: Social Sciences Academic Resource Center (SSARC) Resource Mangers (RMs) report directly to the Director and Associate Director, serving as frontline resource consultants, assisting visitors with resume development, graduate and professional school planning, internship placement, and professional development.

title: Educational Policy Field Studies
description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.

title: Educational Policy Field Studies
description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 195A

title: Educational Policy Field Studies
description: Integrates academic course work with experiential learning; examines the effects of educational policy on urban and suburban schools; explores the relationship between community service and personal academic interests; and develops awareness about the challenges of public education.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI 195B

title: Professional Internship
description: Students apply classroom knowledge through research projects in nonprofit agencies (local, state, and government) and the private sector. They pose solutions to agency-posed questions. Students gain field experience through 50 hours (for 2 units) or 100 (for 4 units).
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Directed Group Study
description: Directed study with Social Science faculty.

title: Individual Study
description: Opportunities to do research and learn new skills outside the normal classroom environment. Students participate in planned research and study activities under a written contract with a supervising UCI instructor. Students may enroll for only one 199 each quarter.

title: Race and Justice Studies Writing Seminar
description: A required writing-intensive seminar conducted by an instructor affiliated with the Race and Justice Studies emphasis. Students with manuscripts on relevant topics will read and critique peer manuscripts, and revise manuscripts toward completion of articles, dissertation chapters, and other publications.
prerequisites_raw: CRM/LAW C260C with a minimum grade of B-

title: Transnational Migration
description: Examines borders and boundaries as material and semiotic constructs. Drawing upon an array of literatures, but loosely situated in U.S. geo/biopolitics, explores transformative troublings of places, spaces, borders, and bodies of all sorts.

title: Special Topics in Social Science
description: Current research in Social Science.

title: Dissertation Research
description: Dissertation research with Social Science faculty.

title: Introduction to Social Ecology
description: Introduction to the ecological paradigm through a consideration of the classic and recent works in human, cultural, and social ecology. Emphasis on the use of the ecological paradigm as an aid in analyzing societal problems and prescribing for their amelioration.

title: Research Design
description: An introduction to the logic behind and methods of designing and conducting research studies in Social Ecology. Topics include how to measure variables of interest, identifying causal relationships, sampling, survey research methods, experiments, quasi-experimental designs, and ethics in research.

title: Statistical Analysis in Social Ecology
description: Introduction to the techniques of statistical analysis in Social Ecology. Topics include probability, statistical inference, significance testing, univariate descriptive statistics, and multivariate analysis from an interdisciplinary perspective.

title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H1E or SOCECOL H20A

title: Honors: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Each quarter focuses on a different topic. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H1F or SOCECOL H20B

title: Critical Issues on the Social Sciences
description: Major themes, methods, and works in the social sciences from an interdisciplinary perspective. Weekly seminars emphasizing development of critical thinking skills and quantitative analysis through written work are integral to the course.

title: Moral Development and Just Communities
description: A three-quarter sequence exploring interpersonal, personal, and social issues based on principles of fairness and justice. Both the living environment of a University residence hall and selected institutions of society are analyzed in terms of moral development theory.

title: Moral Development and Just Communities
description: A three-quarter sequence exploring interpersonal, personal, and social issues based on principles of fairness and justice. Both the living environment of a University residence hall and selected institutions of society are analyzed in terms of moral development theory.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 74A

title: Moral Development and Just Communities
description: A three-quarter sequence exploring interpersonal, personal, and social issues based on principles of fairness and justice. Both the living environment of a University residence hall and selected institutions of society are analyzed in terms of moral development theory.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 74B

title: Special Topics in Social Ecology
description: Special topics courses are offered from time to time. In general they will focus on a topic from interdisciplinary perspectives. Course content varies with the interest of the instructor.

title: Community Archiving in Social Ecology
description: Students are trained in community archiving, oral history, and ethnography in order to produce material for submission to a student-initiated Social Ecology community archive housed in the UC Irvine Special Collections section of the UC Irvine libraries.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 10 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Minimum cumulative GPA above 2.0. Authorization for field study

title: Building, Analyzing, and Sustaining a Digital Media Archive
description: Students are trained in contributing to and managing a digital media archive. Provided an opportunity to use resources in the archive to develop policy proposals to solve real-world problems at the intersection of crime, law, and society.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 10 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement. Minimum cumulative GPA above 2.0. Authorization for field study

title: Advanced Research Methods
description: For students planning to conduct senior research projects or apply to graduate school in social research fields. Topics include reviewing literature, preparing a research proposal, protecting human subjects, citing scholarly work, building measures, estimating sample size, interview and presentation skills.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 10 and SOCECOL 13 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Domestic Violence
description: General perspectives about domestic violence and theoretical accounts about what causes such behavior.

title: Violence in Intimate Relationships
description: Responses to various forms of domestic violence, such as intimate partner violence and child abuse. Covers barriers to reporting to the police, and prosecutors and courts. Human services, such as safety planning for victims, treatment programs, and restorative justice approaches.

title: Nuclear Environments
description: Understanding the impact of the nuclear age on the environment and human health through interrelated developments of nuclear power and nuclear weapons. The early years of weapon development, catastrophic environmental pollution, perils of nuclear power in the U.S. and Russia.

title: Global and International Studies Forum
description: A faculty-student forum featuring lectures from a variety of institutions with discussion issues related to Global and International Studies.

title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability I
description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations. Prepare bibliography.

title: Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability II
description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum is also required. Seminar utilized to analyze forum presentations. Prepare research proposal.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 191A or SOCECOL 186A or EARTHSS 190A

title: Writing/Senior Seminar on Global Sustainability III
description: Students attend weekly seminar to discuss current issues in global sustainability. Weekly attendance at Global Sustainability Forum also is required. Seminar utilized to analyze Forum presentations and to prepare senior research paper. Prepare/write research paper under direction of faculty member.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B . BIO SCI 191B or EARTHSS 190B or SOCECOL 186B . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Advanced Seminar in the Science and Practice of Compassion
description: For students who are accepted into the Global Service Scholars Program. Provides advanced training in empathy and compassion, and prepares students for their summer international field experience.
prerequisites_raw: PSCI 192B

title: Applied Statistics in Social and Behavioral Research
description: Covers statistical techniques used to describe and make generalizations about phenomena represented by data. Hands-on experience in data analysis and interpretation using statistical software (SPSS, STATA) is emphasized. Topics include data visualization, ANOVA, multiple regression, and categorical data analyses.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 13

title: Honors Research
description: Independent work on an individual research project in addition to participation in a mini proseminar in which faculty discuss their ongoing research. Students prepare a written proposal for a research project.

title: Honors Research
description: Independent work on an individual research project in a addition to participation in a mini proseminar in which faculty discuss their ongoing research. Students prepare a written proposal for a research project.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL H190A

title: Honors Research
description: Students write up their honors research project (H190A-B) and prepare an oral report which is presented at the honors seminar.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL H190B . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Naturalistic Field Research
description: Introduction to alternative models of experiential learning and to various methods of observation, assessment, and evaluation. Introduction to the nature of organizations and ethical issues that emerge from research and intervention in natural settings.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 10 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Field Study
description: Community engagement to facilitate civic education through field research experience, social intervention, and professionalization. Small group instruction, discussion, writing, and presentations synthesizing students’ experiences in the field with theory, paradigms, and ideas learned about in their course work.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 10

title: Advanced Field Study
description: While completing 8 hours of field work per week, students become acquainted with the goals and activities of their placement and work closely with the placement supervisor and AFS instructor to identify the scope of a community project.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 10 . Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required

title: Advanced Field Study
description: While completing 8 hours of field work per week, students implement their research project through data collection and observations which allow them to reflect on, apply, and synthesize their academic training through observations and experiences at the placement.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 195A . Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required

title: Advanced Field Study
description: While completing 8 hours per week of field work, students write and finalize their AFS Client Project in consultation with the placement and the FS instructor, and make a final written and oral presentation to the placement and invited guests.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 195B . Acceptance to Advanced Field Study required. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Field Study Writing Seminar
description: Community engagement to promote civic education through field research experience, and the opportunity to study social issues and the environments where they occur. Develop discipline-specific writing and communication skills, methodology, and integrate information from multiple sources.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 10 . Cumulative UC GPA of 2.0. Authorization is required. Successful completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Directed Studies
description: Directed study with Social Ecology faculty.

title: Special Studies
description: Special Studies with Social Ecology faculty.

title: Data Analysis
description: Provides an appreciation and understanding of statistics necessary to conduct applied research. Topics include approaches to and presentation of data, robust statistics, standardization techniques, multivariate regression, and analysis of variance.

title: Data Analysis
description: Provides an appreciation and understanding of statistics necessary to conduct applied research. Topics include approaches to and presentation of data, robust statistics, standardization techniques, multivariate regression, and analysis of variance.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 264A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Analysis of Survival Data
description: Provides an introduction to survival analysis methods for the analysis of change in discrete dependent variables. Focuses on data collection strategies for obtaining longitudinal data and continuous-time hazards models. Communicates the variety and power of multivariate hazard models.

title: Structural Equation Modeling I
description: The general structural equation model is developed including path models, recursive and nonrecursive structural models, multiple indicator models, and confirmatory factor models. Use of LISREL and other software for estimating model parameters is covered.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 264A with a minimum grade of B- and SOCECOL 264B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Structural Equation Modeling II: Longitudinal and Advanced Topics
description: Provides hands-on experience with longitudinal and advanced structural equation models and is of interest to students from a range of disciplines. Topics covered include confirmatory factor, latent growth curve, general growth mixture, and multi-level modeling.
prerequisites_raw: SOCECOL 272A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Special Topics in Social Ecology
description: Topics covered vary with interests of the instructor.

prerequisites_raw: Advancement to candidacy

title: Doctoral Dissertation Research & Writing
description: Dissertation research with Social Ecology faculty.
prerequisites_raw: Advancement to Candidacy

title: Fundamentals of Spanish
description: First quarter of Fundaments of Spanish that helps students develop basic reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish. Delivered in a hybrid format.
prerequisites_raw: Placement into SPANISH 1A

title: Fundamentals of Spanish
description: Second quarter of Fundaments of Spanish that helps students develop basic reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish. Delivered in a hybrid format.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 1A with a minimum grade of C-. Placement into SPANISH 1B is also accepted

title: Fundamentals of Spanish
description: Third quarter of Fundaments of Spanish that helps students develop basic reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish. Delivered in a hybrid format.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 1B with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH S1AB with a minimum grade of B. Placement into SPANISH 1C is also accepted

title: Fundamentals of Spanish
description: First half of first-year Spanish in an intensified form. Communicative approach with emphasis on conversational skills.
prerequisites_raw: Placement into SPANISH 1A

title: Fundamentals of Spanish
description: Second half of first-year Spanish in an intensified form. Communicative approach with emphasis on conversational skills.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH S1AB with a minimum grade of C or SPANISH 1A with a minimum grade of B or SPANISH 1B with a minimum grade of C. Placement into SPANISH 1B or SPANISH 1C is also accepted

title: Intermediate Spanish
description: First quarter of Intermediate Spanish that helps students further develop their reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish and a cultural understanding of the Spanish-speaking world. Delivered in a hybrid format.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 1C with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH S1BC with a minimum grade of C-. Placement into SPANISH 2A is also accepted

title: Intermediate Spanish
description: Second quarter of Intermediate Spanish that helps students further develop their reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish and a cultural understanding of the Spanish-speaking world. Delivered in a hybrid format.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 2A with a minimum grade of C-. Placement into SPANISH 2B is also accepted

title: Intermediate Spanish
description: Third quarter of Intermediate Spanish that helps students further develop their reading, listening, speaking, and writing skills in Spanish and a cultural understanding of the Spanish-speaking world. Delivered in a hybrid format.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 2AB with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH 2B with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH S2AB with a minimum grade of B. Placement into SPANISH 2C is also accepted

title: Intermediate Spanish
description: First half of second-year Spanish in an intensified form. Conversation, reading, and composition skills are developed using texts of literary and social interest. Emphasis on grammar review.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 1C with a minimum grade of C or SPANISH S1BC with a minimum grade of C. Placement into SPANISH 2A is also accepted

title: Intermediate Spanish
description: Second half of second-year Spanish in an intensified form. Conversation, reading, and composition skills are developed using texts of literary and social interest. Emphasis on grammar review.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 2B with a minimum grade of C or SPANISH S2AB with a minimum grade of C or SPANISH 2A with a minimum grade of B. Placement into SPANISH 2B or SPANISH 2C is also accepted

title: US Latino Communities
description: Focuses on intermediate to advanced grammar and composition. Emphasis is placed on key elements of grammar, which constitutes about 70 percent of the curriculum, and composition writing, which constitutes the remaining 30 percent.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 2C with a minimum grade of C- or SPANISH S2BC with a minimum grade of C or AP Spanish Language Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 3 is also accepted

title: Heritage Spanish: Latinidades en California
description: Designed for students who grew up speaking Spanish in their homes and who need additional practice writing in Spanish. Delivered in a hybrid format.
prerequisites_raw: AP Spanish Language Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 3H

title: Topics in Latin America, U.S. Latino, and Iberian Cultures
description: Introduction to the culture of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds (Europe, Latin America, U.S., Africa). May focus on any time period. Taught in English.

title: Mexico and Central America: A Survey
description: Panoramic view of Mexico and Central America examining key texts throughout history. Shows the richness of the culture, and an appraisal of various forms of representation, including images, chronicles, novels, essays, poems, and a film. Taught in English.

title: The Culture of the Visual Image in Latin America
description: A survey of visual forms of expression which have endured through more than five centuries of pre-colonial, colonial, and independent Latin America. Forms to be treated in the class include painting, monuments, sculpture, urban planning, graffiti, comics, and photography.

title: Latinx, Multilingualism, and Social Justice
description: Explores the role of multilingualism (Spanish, indigenous languages, Latino English) in Latinx social justice movements in the United States with an emphasis on California. Course is taught in English.

title: Fundamentals of Spanish (with Emphasis on Reading)
description: Designed for students interested in acquiring a solid reading knowledge of Spanish, and to facilitate the understanding and translating of Spanish texts covering a variety of disciplines. Does not fulfill any undergraduate foreign language requirement. Taught in English.
prerequisites_raw: Does not serve as prerequisite for any higher-level Spanish courses

title: Introduction to Iberian Literature and Culture
description: Introduction to the major authors and movements of Iberian literature and culture from the Middle Ages to the present.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Introductory Studies to Latin American Literature and Culture
description: A historical overview of Latin American literature and culture mainly focused on canonical texts. Topics include colonialism and postcolonialism, the nation, indigenismo, gender, and literary movements. Also introduces literary analysis, research methods, and cultural critique.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Spanish Communication
description: Designed to help students develop Spanish oral skills by exposing them to different verbal Spanish language registers. Special emphasis placed on abilities essential to professional or academic careers. Intended for Spanish majors as an important component of their overall education.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Advanced Spanish Grammar
description: Designed for students who have demonstrated a substantial level of proficiency in their studies of the Spanish language. Takes thorough approach to advanced grammatical problems, in order to assist students in their mastery of the elements of the Spanish language.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Topics in Spanish for the Professions
description: Taught in Spanish to promote linguistic competencies, intercultural awareness, and understanding of local Latino communities’ needs. Provides resources to carry out professional tasks and build meaningful community-based relationships in the health, legal, and business fields.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Topics in Peninsular Literature and Cultures
description: Topics in Peninsular literature and cultures.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: U.S. Latino Literature and Cultures
description: Focuses on aspects of literature, art, cultural production, and history of the multifaceted Latino cultures that have developed within the United States. Focuses on one group, such as Caribbean Americans, Chicanos, Central Americans, or a comparative perspective of several groups.

title: Spanish Phonetics
description: Introduction to fundamental notions of Spanish phonetics. Particular attention paid to problems of pronunciation that arise in native and non-native speakers of Spanish due to interference between Spanish and English. Phonology (the system that underlies phonetics) and Spanish dialectology included.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Introduction to Spanish Linguistics
description: Introduces students to the scientific study of the Spanish language with a focus on its sound system, word components, word order as well as second language acquisition and language variation. Class is delivered in a hybrid format.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Textual Analysis and Interpretation
description: Focus on analysis and interpretation of literary texts. Emphasis on narrative, poetry, theater/performance, and visual media. Introduces students to major currents in theoretical thought, such as cultural studies, postmodernism, and others. Oral presentations and short essays required. Taught in Spanish.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Topics in Golden Age Literature and Culture
description: Golden Age Literature in Spain, including the Renaissance and Baroque periods. Works of poetry, narrative, and theater. Historical and cultural background.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Topics in 20th and 21st Century Spanish Literature and Culture
description: 20th century Spanish authors. Works of poetry, narrative, or theater. Historical context of the period and principles of literary theory.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Topics in Latin American Literature and Culture of the 20th Century
description: Topics in Latin American literature and culture of the 20th century.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Topics in Chicano Literature and Culture
description: Studies in selected areas of Chicano/Latino Studies. Topics addressed vary each quarter. Taught in English.

title: Topics in Literature in Translation
description: Study of texts by modern and contemporary Peninsular, Latin American, and/or U.S. Latino writers in translation. Taught in English. Not applicable toward Spanish major or minor requirements.

title: Topics in Luso-Hispanic Film Studies
description: Study of Peninsular, Latin-American, and/or U.S. Latino film. Taught in English or Spanish.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Topics in Peninsular Literature and Culture
description: Selection of representative topics in Spanish and/or Portuguese literature and culture.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Topics in Latin American Literature and Culture
description: Selection of representative topics in the history of Latin American literature and culture.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Selected Topics in Spanish Linguistics
description: Major topics in Spanish linguistics.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 3 or SPANISH 3H or AP Spanish Literature Exam with a minimum score of 4. Placement into SPANISH 101A is also accepted

title: Colloquium
description: Specialized, discussion-based course dealing primarily with a research topic that reflects the instructor's current intellectual interests. Required oral presentation(s) and final research paper. Limited to 15 students.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 101A and SPANISH 101B and SPANISH 119

title: Independent Study
description: Research paper required.

title: Topics in Twentieth Century
description: Topics in twentieth-century Spanish literature and culture.

title: Topics in Twentieth-Century Latin America
description: Topics in twentieth-century Latin America.

title: Topics in Literary Theory I
description: Traces the development of Western literary critical principles from Aristotle to the twentieth century through selected readings of key figures in intellectual history (Aristotle, St. Augustine, Descartes, Kant, Hegel, Marx, Nietzsche, William James, Freud).

title: Special Topics in Theory
description: Focus on issues related to critical theory, theory of literature, cultural criticism and visual arts as they pertain specifically to Latin America, Spain, Portugal, and Brazil. Topics vary. Examples: Latin American cultural studies; theory, film, and media in post-war Spain.

title: Seminar in Spanish
description: Topics in Spanish.

title: Professionalization Seminar
description: Addresses the transition from graduate student to professional with a Ph.D. in Spanish. Covers formative stages in the progress of graduate students towards their degrees, as well as help with the preparation for a successful professional career.

title: Professionalization Seminar
description: Addresses the transition from graduate student to professional with a Ph.D. in Spanish. Covers formative stages in the progress of graduate students towards their degrees, as well as helps with the preparation for a successful professional career.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 260A

title: Professionalization Seminar
description: Addresses the transition from graduate student to professional with a Ph.D. in Spanish. Covers formative stages in the progress of graduate students towards their degrees, as well as helps with the preparation for a successful professional career.
prerequisites_raw: SPANISH 260B

title: World Language Teaching Methodologies: Theory and Practice
description: Graduate seminar introducing theory and world language teaching, with a focus on Spanish, grounding instructional techniques in Instructed Second Language Acquisition. Emphasizes reflective, evidence-based language teaching pedagogy, communicative and task-based language teaching, and professional development.

title: Spanish Teaching Methodology I
description: Required for graduate students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese who will teach in the Spanish Language Program. Prepares graduate students to develop effective teaching practices that promote learning Spanish as a second language.

title: Spanish Teaching Methodology II
description: Required for graduate students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese who will teach in the Spanish Language Program. Prepares graduate students to develop effective teaching practices that promote learning Spanish as a second language.

title: Creative Writing Workshop in Spanish/English
description: Discussion of theory and practice of creative writing. Focus on critical analysis of participant's work in progress. Texts may be written in Spanish and/or English and may be written in poetry or prose format.

title: Individual Study
description: Individual Study.

title: Directed Reading
description: Directed Reading in Spanish.

title: Teaching Practicum
description: Teaching Practicum.

title: Dissertation Research
description: Dissertation Research.

title: Social Policy and Public Service
description: An introduction to the basic theories and principles of public policy. Students examine various influences on the development of public policy and the principle actors in the process, and learn to identify tools and techniques employed in policy making.

title: Race and Ethnicity
description: Focuses on racial and ethnic relations in the United States and compares them with those found in other societies. Analyzes the conditions that favor either cooperation and integration or rivalry, tension, and conflict. Appraises strategies for reducing and resolving conflicts.

title: Critical Investigations into Humanitarianism in Africa
description: Explores the complex phenomenon of aid to Africa (emergency and development aid), and the representational, cultural, historical, and other reasons why some participants and many observers critique it. Students occasionally engage with peers and faculty in African institutions.

title: Honors Research Workshop
description: Student develops a 10–15-page prospectus of research for the honors thesis which includes: the research question, literature review, methods of investigation, and bibliography. Student selects a faculty mentor who will supervise thesis research and writing in winter and spring.

title: Honors Thesis Research
description: The student initiates and completes data collection for the honors thesis. A faculty mentor provides supervision and feedback on thesis chapters.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H190A or SPPS H190A

title: Honors Thesis
description: The student completes, with the approval of the faculty mentor, an honors thesis containing: statement of the problem, literature review, research hypotheses, methods of investigation, results, discussion, and bibliography.
prerequisites_raw: SOC SCI H190B or SPPS H190B . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement
